utterances.text: Well, you see, what you just said really contradicts Article 10 of the Law on Internal Affairs; subparagraph 2. says that: "The minister of the interior cannot issue orders to other structures within the ministry." That's what you just said. But that legal provision says that in times disturbance of public peace and order, the minister can direct authorised officials to carry out certain activities. So why do you say that the minister of the interior cannot issue orders to other structures within the ministry? Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I'm making a distinction between the way in which a decision is built and made, and the formal issuance and signing of a decision as a formal act.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understood that response. Are you saying that under Article 10 of the Law on Internal Affairs subparagraph 2, the minister cannot issue instructions to authorised officials in the ministry, including the director of public security?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This competency of the minister, or authorisation to issue such act, such order, is what it is. But the way in which the decision is made, the way in which the decision is then executed are established by separate acts. The decision is brought by the collegium. It is not a decision by the minister himself, a decision that the minister alone can make, because the minister does not have all the elements necessary to make the assessment. This is why the minister needs a collegium. The minister can issue an order after the decision is made.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you saying, Professor, now, and is it your evidence, that again, are you saying that in a meeting of the collegium that the members of the collegium are supposed to make decisions based on consensus? Is that what you're saying, that that's how the decision is made, and then after that the minister just issues a piece of paper saying, "My decision is this"? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding of the matters, but I stated before, that I can't give my opinion with regards to the work of the collegium because I haven't analysed that and I have never participated in the work of the collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Well, then I'm confused why a moment ago you discussed how the collegium functions, but I'm going to leave it alone for now. I will move to another topic. Professor Taseva, after the Ohrid Framework Agreement was signed on the 13th of August, 2001, you're aware, aren't you, that the NLA undertook to demobilise its ranks and to turn in its weapons --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, there is something I forgot to do. Your Honour, I forgot to tender the video-clip that we saw a few minutes ago. That was 65 ter 1117.6, if I could tender that, please, so I don't forget it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours. I don't know what is the relevance of this video-clip, considering, as we heard, that was a speech of Mr. Boskoski made within a political campaign of his party in the summer of 2002. So that goes beyond the scope of the indictment and also beyond his ministerial duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, this entire discussion with this witness has been about the powers and authorities of the minister and whether they are expressly restricted by the laws or not, and this is one example, Your Honours, where they are not expressly restricted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is not the issue, Mr. Saxon. The issue is whether the video itself is relevant. The fact that he made a political speech is one that is demonstrated by the video is accepted by the witness, and there has been discussion about his capacity to do so. But is the content of the speech or something about the video material in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In this case. Well, for example, at 1638, Mr. Boskoski, in referring to the events in 2001, refers to the fact how he and the prime minister, Ljubco Georgievski, were there in Tetovo during the crisis period in 2001; specifically referring to the prime minister, not the president. At 22:16, he also refers to the fact that the prime minister was in Tetovo with the policemen who were defending Macedonia at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P577, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You are aware, I believe, Professor Taseva, that after the Ohrid Agreement was signed on the 13th of August, 2001 the NLA undertook to demobilised its ranks and turn in its weapons by 26 September 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, I can. It is from the member.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And the process of collecting NLA weapons was accomplished with the assistance of NATO forces in an operation in August and September 2001 called Essential Harvest. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness what is Exhibit P00083, please. That is the Law on Amnesty, and this will be available in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You can see, Professor, that this law was published in the Official Gazette on Friday, the 8th of March, 2002, and it was the decree for proclaiming the Law on Amnesty which was adopted by the assembly of the Republic of Macedonia on the 7th of March, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you see how, for example, in the first paragraph, the first line, it says: "This law exempts from prosecution, discontinues the criminal proceedings ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then, in the English, in the last two lines of that paragraph: "... for whom there is a reasonable doubt that they have prepared or committed criminal acts related to the conflict in the year 2001 conclusive of 26 September 2001." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could we see more of the bottom of the page. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, in the next paragraph, you see a reference to persons who have prepared or committed criminal acts; and then, two subparagraphs down, it says: "The criminal proceedings for criminal acts pursuant to the Criminal Code and other laws," at the end, "are discontinued." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we can take a look at the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There's nothing in the Law on Amnesty that refers to disciplinary proceedings, does it?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there isn't anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you aware that in its reasons for passing the Law on Amnesty, the government of Macedonia noted that the amnesty law covers persons who participated in the conflict and who voluntarily gave up their weapons by 26 September 2001? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, doesn't that sound, then, that the Law on Amnesty was really directed at members of the NLA, not at members of the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law does not make any distinction between the individuals comprised by it, so everyone is who participated in the actions. The law speaks of citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, people with legal residence and individuals who have families or property and regarding which there is a suspicion and then, as you read it. So there is no distinction with regards to the capacity of the citizens, ethnic, religious, official, or any other capacity of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I understand that. But we've been talking about the interpretation of laws for several days now; and, first of all, would you agree with me that laws are often the extension of politics, of political situations?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The laws are the expression of the will of the politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in 2001, the members of the NLA, they were considered to be terrorists and outlaws, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many terms used during that period. Outlaws also was among them; terrorists, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And many NLA members, in particular NLA leaders, were living a clandestine life, weren't they? They were in hiding from the authorities and institutions of the state. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, can you give us your opinion as someone who lived through that time and is certainly aware of the events of that time.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm this because there is the way in which many of the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm asking you about members of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, would it be fair to say that many members of the NLA were separated and isolated at least from the ethnic Macedonian population?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what do you base that answer on?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I don't have any first-hand knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So why did you answer "no"?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I can't say in the affirmative and because my personal experience does not confirm anything of that nature. So I'm saying no, because that is my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But if I understand you, you're saying really that you don't know. Is that what you're saying? Are you saying "I can't say in the affirmative." So you don't know; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Throughout the crisis time in 2001, members of the army and the police, they continued to live as fully -- fully active, lawful citizens of Macedonia, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All citizens in the Republic of Macedonia, in that period of time, lived as active, lawful citizens of the Republic of Macedonia. There were no restrictions for anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it your evidence, Professor Taseva, that the fighters of the NLA in 2001 were living as active, lawful citizens of the Republic of Macedonia? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And by the same token, the members of the security forces would also have been living as active, lawful citizens, right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, then, why, in paragraph 128 in your report, in the first sentence, do you say: "The main purpose of the law was to ensure that peace could return to the country and that 'those involved in the fighting could be reintegrated into society.'"? Why did people need to be reintegrated into society if they had never left society? How does that work?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is it a political decision at hand, and it means that everyone who participated or took part must be reintegrated. There is no restrictions as to one or another side which needs to be reintegrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question. Can you answer my question, please?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this conflict, which had two parties to it, here it is stated those who were involved should be reintegrated, the ones, the others, and everyone together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, you see, in your expert report, you said: "And that those involved in the fighting could be reintegrated into society." But you've just told us that members of the NLA, the NLA fighters and the fighters of the Macedonian security forces, were never separated from Macedonian society. So I'm just trying to understand what that sentence means in your report or how it is consistent with what you have told us today?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This sentence denotes what is incorporated in the political documents of the times, where it -- reintegration of all citizens of the society was discussed, to continue the normal course of life and work, regardless of who belonged to what side or in what capacity took part in those activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And regardless of the fact that people had never left society. They had never been separated from society.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. They were never separated from the society. But in the society, a condition was created whereby together the citizens, the politicians, and the international community assessed required measures for overcoming. This is why the Ohrid Agreement was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the second sentence of paragraph 128. You say: "It was also," in other words, it the was the purpose of the amnesty law, "was also to serve a societal purpose in avoiding vengeance by all, institution or otherwise." Then you cite to a exhibit, in footnote 141, Exhibit 1D185.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we see that exhibit, please. Can we enlarge the Macedonian version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can read the second paragraph in the Macedonian version to us, Professor. It begins with: "The Ministry of Interior." Can you read that to us out loud, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Ministry of Interior guarantees that it will not arrest, detain, or bring in citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, former members of the NLA, who voluntarily hand in their weapons by 26 September 2001."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is dated the 10th of December, 2001. Professor, there was no requirement for members of the Macedonian police or army to turn in their weapons by 26 September 2001, was there?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an action for collecting weapons from the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Professor, isn't it understood that action was intended to collect the weapons that were in the possession of the so-called NLA? Can you just answer "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please turn to what is Exhibit P00572. This will be at tab 29, binder 1. Can we turn to the next page, please, in both versions. You see it is entitled: Criminal charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You'll see, Professor, this is a criminal charge issued by the Ministry of Interior on the 24th of July, 2001. It's being sent to the public prosecutor of Republic of Macedonia and the basic public prosecutor. You see, for example, in the English version on the first page, it's against Ali Ahmeti, who is described as being actively in the organisation, function, and activity of the so-called UCK.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see at the end, in the English version, at the end of that first long paragraph, it's referring to possibility of crimes -- criminal act of terrorism against Mr. Ali Ahmeti, and then followed by similar language regarding to Fazli Veliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Similar language related to Gzim Ostreni, Musa Demiri, persons who were known to be leaders of the NLA. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 14, please. If we could have the same version in the Macedonian version, please, for Professor Taseva, and the next page in the Macedonian version, please. One more page, please, and one more page. We need to go to the same page as we see in the English. It should be the second-to-the-last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So, you see, here we see the proposal, Professor, that to pursue the perpetrators of the criminal acts against the reported suspects. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And to start of criminal procedure. Then the special proposal, in the next paragraph, is that custody be ordered for these suspects. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we see the bottom of the Macedonian version, please. Can we go to the next page in both versions, and the next -- the last page in the Macedonian version?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So we see that this was -- these criminal charged were signed by the director of public security at that time, Mr. Goran Mitevski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to show what you is 65 ter number 1156.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's in binder 1, tab number 30, and I don't know if it would save time for the witness to look at the hard copy or not, if the usher could assist. I see it's coming up now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is, Professor -- it's a bit hard to see it all. It is a request for an investigation by the -- to extend an investigation by the public prosecutor against these same leaders of the UCK, and it is dated the 8th of October, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So we see that it is submitted by the deputy public prosecutor, Mr. Marko Zrlevski. So, here we see, Professor, an example where, in August of 2001, the investigation against NLA leaders was continuing, right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This proposal to extended investigation is dated, I believe, the 8th of August -- excuse me, the 8th of October, 2001. I misspoke before. My question should be: This is an example where, as of October 2001, the investigation against NLA leaders was continuing, right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Here the procedure is still in the preliminary phase in the public prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that's in spite of the fact that, at that time, people were expecting that, eventually, an amnesty law would be enacted, right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The right to decide whether an activity would fall under this law falls on the courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question. By October 2001, it was generally expected in the Macedonian public that, at some point, there would be a Law on Amnesty enacted, right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P578, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness what is 65 ter 1157. This is at -- in binder 1 at tab 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is a decision dated the 15th of October, 2001, whereby the investigative judge of the Basic Court Skopje agrees to conduct the investigation against these same leaders of the NLA. Do you see that, Professor?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So there we see the decision on the last page, that during the investigation material and verbal evidence shall be obtained, et cetera, to decide whether an indictment should be submitted against the accused. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P579, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It would, Your Honour. I am aware of the time and I really tried very hard to finish in two sessions. Obviously, I did not succeed. I believe I might be able to finish in half an hour in one more session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Our extension of time to a full hour and a half would enable you to have another three quarters of an hour, as a rough indication, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We resume at 1.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Before I re-begin my questions, I need to alert the Chamber and the parties to a mistake that the Prosecution made during the last session. You'll recall that a video-clip was admitted as Exhibit P00577. The 65 ter number of that video-clip was actually 1117.7, not 1117.6 as the Chamber was informed. And because I had numbers transposed, I also gave some incorrect, incorrect, information about the date of that speech. The speech that was -- the video-clip of the speech that was admitted as P577 was given by Mr. Boskoski during the electoral campaign on the 28th of August, 2002, not on the 29th of July, 2002, in Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we please show the witness what is 65 ter 1152, please, and this is at tab 91 in the second Prosecution binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You'll see this is another -- well, this is a indictment that is being submitted, Professor Taseva, on the 6th of March, 2002, by the public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down to the bottom, more towards the bottom of the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see, for example, in paragraph 1, this is an indictment against Mr. Skodran Idrizi. And, in the middle of that paragraph, we see he is in pre-trial detention based on the decision of the investigative judge from Basic Court II in Skopje. Do you see that, Professor?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see several more persons listed who are listed as fugitives, yeah; although, it appears to say that pre-trial detention is recommended when those persons are found, do you see that, for the other persons listed on the first page?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please, in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, on the following page, we see several more persons who are listed in this indictment, and I believe each one of them is a fugitive, but pre-trial detention is recommended at the time of their capture. Do you see that, Professor Taseva?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we agree that, at least in most cases, these gentlemen would have what we call Albanian surnames?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's right; at least, this is what it seems.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please, in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And here is the suggestion for the indictment. There's a few more persons on the third page also with Albanian surnames. And, again, in the middle of the page, we see a suggestion for an indictment against a minor named Fadilj Ferati nicknamed Diljo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we also agree, Professor Taseva, that, in a democratic society, police officers play a special role and -- due to their powers and authority? Can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have the role to carry out the tasks as assigned by law. Everyone who works for the state administration can be said to have a special role.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, yes, but if we speak about the police in particular, since they have the responsibility of protecting the public peace and order, they also have a special relationship of trust with the public, don't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if the purposes of the amnesty law are to promote peace and reconciliation, wouldn't it undermine the purposes of the amnesty law if police officers, those persons who are supposed to have that -- persons who are in that special position of trust towards the public, if police officers who committed serious acts of misconduct are allowed to continue performing the same duties and responsibilities, wouldn't that undermine the entire purpose of the Law on Amnesty?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am attempting to understand, so this is why I have to read it again. I really cannot respond to a question formulated in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, then I'll try to reformulate it. You told us before that one of the main purposes of the amnesty law was to promote peace and reconciliation. So my question is: Well, if police officers are not disciplined for their acts of misconduct, they are essentially given a certain level of immunity, aren't they, first of all?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you are not right in saying this, that members of the police enjoyed some sort of immunity, because the Law on Amnesty does not make any distinctions among citizens on any basis. This is why the provisions of this law pertain to all citizens of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But if police officers -- I misspoke before. I should have used the word "impunity," not "immunity." But if police officers are not held accountable for their disciplinary violations, then how would public trust that is so important for any process of peace and reconciliation be advanced?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the same manner in which many were amnestied, people who took part in the events of that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know any police officers who were amnestied?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know any specific person who was amnestied because I do not know them personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, you're taking my question very literally. Do you know of, have you heard about any police officers who were amnestied, who received amnesty for acts committed in 2001?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that there are persons who received amnesty; but who they are, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You heard that, but you don't have any more information that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no more information than that the law is applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to move to a slightly different topic. Can we show the witness what is Exhibit P530, please, on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see this is a file, and it involves a disciplinary matter for a man named Peco Josevski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the last page, please, in both languages?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You can see, Professor Taseva, that disciplinary punishment was imposed against this individual. And in the second-to-the-last paragraph we see a sentence that stands alone, and it say this is -- actually the third-to-the paragraph.: "Against this decision, within eight days after the reception of the same, the employee has the right to object to the commission for arbitration at the second level of the area of labour at the government of the Republic of Macedonia through this Ministry of Interior." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So, in other words, the employee has the right, within eight days, to appeal this decision. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then it says: "The objection, or the appeal, does not prevent the execution of this decision." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So these decisions go into force, even while an appeal of the decision is pending. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how it is regulated by law in the collective agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is a "yes"?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this is so because it is regulated in this manner by procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to talk to you about the Law on Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn to your report, to paragraph 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Paragraph 18 says: "In 2001, the president could also exercise his authority over the police forces. A new Law on Defence was adopted in June 2001 which circumscribed the power of the president over police forces. "However, and in practice, the president continued to perform his constitutional authority over both the army and the police forces of the Republic. The by-laws necessary for the complete enforcement of the new Law on Defence had not been adopted." What you're saying there in paragraph 18 is that, in practice, during the summer of 2001, the president continued to exercise his authority over both the army and the police. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness what is Exhibit P464. Your Honours, this is the book: The War in Macedonia. In the ERN range, the English ERN range, N006-3017 to N006-3033, can we go to page 8 in the English version. In the Macedonian version, this will be page 107 in e-court -- actually, 106. I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you see this subheading that says: "Orders the use of the police during martial law to support the army." Do you see that in bold? Do you see that in bold, Professor?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it; except, I do not understand the English translation. In Macedonian, it is stated: "Orders the use of the police during a state of war as support of the army."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. By the way, a state of war was never declared in Macedonia during 2001, was it?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not proclaimed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you look at the paragraph below that bold subtitle, we see a paragraph beginning with: "Since martial law was not..." -- or I suppose it should say in English: "Since a state of war was not declared." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It reads like this, and in the moment we'll have to go to the next page in the Macedonian version: "Since a state of war was not declared, the police was not under Joint Command and acted independently. One can only imagine what the situation is like when two ministers from the same government (MVR, Ministry of Interior and MO, Ministry of Defence) have two armed components at their disposal, one of which is 'commanded,' by the prime minister through the minister of the interior, while the other is under the command of the president of the Republic through the Defence minister." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So the authors of this book are indicating that during the crisis time in 2001 there were effectively two chains of command: One from the army going up to the president, the commander in chief; and the police going up to the prime minister through the minister of the interior. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, but that is the indication, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, he's talking about two ministers from the same government having two armed components at their disposal, right? One is commanded by the prime minister through the minister of the interior; and the other is commanded by the president of the Republic through the Defence minister. You see that, right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness, please, Exhibit P402, and this is the book, My Battle for Macedonia, by Mr. Boskoski. And if we can go, please, quickly to page -- page 12 in the Macedonian e-court version and page 12 in the English e-court version. And in the English version, if we can focus on the paragraph at the bottom of the page, please. And if we can focus on the same paragraph in the Macedonian version, beginning: "From the manager post in the office ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see there's a paragraph that says, starts: "From the manager post." Do you see that, Professor?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in that paragraph, a few lines down, we see: "The situation escalated and the circumstances led to a government reconstruction where I was appointed minister of the interior. The prime minister, who, on several occasions, publicly demanded a proclamation of a state of ...," and it says "martial law" in English. I don't know if it says "state of war" in the Macedonian original: "... in the country, in order to quickly, efficiently, and professionally put an end to the intruders, to which demand the president of the country did not react. So the prime minister wanted a more sophisticated action in that situation by the Macedonian security forces, which greatly depended on the Ministry of Internal Affairs top management." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this section of this book would be consistent with the section that I read to from The War in Macedonia a moment or two ago, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree. I can't comment on those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why can't you comment on those issues? You commented on the Law on Defence and the role of the president and the role of the minister of the interior, so why can't you comment now?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I commented upon and what is advanced in my report is based on the documents that I saw and the acts, laws, and by-laws that I analysed. These here are books written by authors who advance something, I don't know what, in those books, whether those are their personal experiences or story telling or dreams. So I can't comment. Therefore, I wouldn't venture comments on something that I see for the first time now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay, Professor --

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regards to my report, I know precisely why those words and conclusions were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Professor, moving on to a different topic. Briefly, can you tell us how, during the crisis time in 2001, members of the press and media communicated with the members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. How did the media obtain its information from the Ministry of Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to put a few points to you, Professor Taseva, if I may, please. I'd like to put to you the proposition that you have interpreted the rules and the laws related to the Ministry of Internal Affairs in a highly restrictive manner, which is not logical and is not consistent with the actual practice of the Ministry of Internal Affairs as it was in 2001. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree. I commented upon the issues as I felt the comments were deserved.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I put it to you, Professor, that the rules and law -- that the Law on Internal Affairs and other rules and laws that affect the functioning of the Ministry of Internal Affairs demonstrate that, in 2001, the ministry was a very centralised structure with a strict hierarchy, with the minister at the top of that hierarchy. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I suggest to you that the police department and the criminal police were answerable to the minister through the head of the bureau for public security. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Pursuant to the law, the minister has the competencies over the work of the ministry. So he has to be responsible for the work of the bureau also, but the work of the bureau is organised and coordinated by the director of the bureau.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I put it to you that, in 2001, the minister of internal affairs had effective oversight over police operations as demonstrated by his various orders and decisions. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I put it to you, Professor, that, in 2001, Minister Boskoski did not narrowly follow the black letter law and was in control over police units within the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I put it to you, Professor, that, in 2001, important matters were not resolved in the Ministry of Interior without the approval of the minister. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't agree with this because I don't have the facts to support this position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I put it to you, Professor, that, in 2001, Minister Boskoski had the power and authority to establish police units and even engage police units to go into combat without strict formalities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Professor Taseva. I will take up from the most recent questions put to you by my learned friend. My colleague showed to you a book by some authors; and in relation to that, he put to you that there was a dual line chain of command in 2002 and you did not accept that. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown 65 ter 1D1268, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The year is "2001," not "2002."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can Article 1 be shown of the relevant law on special rights of members of the security forces of the ministry of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Rather, please read out or read Article 2. Can you read that Article in Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Members of the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia, as specified by this law, are soldier serving conscription military service, professional soldier, military officer, and a civilian serving within the permanent force of the army district of the Republic of Macedonia, uniformed person within the Ministry of Internal Affairs, as well as individuals with special competency and authorisations employed in the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Interior."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There's no need to read any further. Professor Taseva, does this description of who makes up the security forces tally with your position whereby these were single forces of the Republic of Macedonia in 2001?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To me this feels like a misleading use of the evidence because this is a document that I believe is dated January 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it relates to the previous year 2002, and to the rights these individuals enjoyed in the previous year.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if we could be pointed to that part of the text that says that, Your Honour, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under paragraph 2, it says: Participation in the defence of independence, territorial integrity, and sovereignty of the Republic of Macedonia, and in the prevention of violent destruction of the democratic institutions, determined with the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia, in view of paragraph 1 of this Article, this means in an organised activity of the members of the security forces in armed activities against armed extremist and paramilitary groups." I'm really sorry, Your Honours, not to have the entire law here to be able to read it out to you, but paragraph 1 deals with a specific date and it says they are set up in the constitution of Macedonia from 2nd of January, 2002. In the text it says, member of the security forces. But the translation erroneously reads "1st of January 2002"; while in Macedonian text it readings: "as of 1st of January, 2000."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Residovic; and if there is some issue about that, it can be taken up on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Perhaps Professor Taseva should now be shown the document dated 21st of June 2001, which is 65 ter 1D529. Page is 1D4809. The English version being 1D8176.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, do you see at the top of the document that the date is the 21st of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you'll agree with me that this is after the new law was, in fact, enforced?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who is the issuing authority of this enactment of this combat order?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As is written on the order itself, that is the Ministry of Defence, General Staff of the army of Republic of Macedonia, command of the security forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And to whom is this document addressed? This is an abbreviation of --

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: ESZ, units for special tasks within the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is a direct combat order from the General Staff to one of the units of the Ministry of Interior. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Taseva, does this document, too, confirm your position according to which the police units were under the command of the army in the course of 2001 and after the new Law on Defence was passed?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Professor Taseva, my learned friend asked you about the return of weapons by the 26th of September 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in addition to NLA, were there other Albanian groups and otherwise in possession of illegal weapons at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that all citizens were duty-bound do return weapons. Did this order refer to the return of illegally held weapons or legally held weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All citizens that had illegal weapons needed to return those during that action.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The army and the police, were they in possession of illegal weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That action did not pertain to the army or the police at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend showed you a number of documents relating to the so-called Mavrovo's worker's case. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were familiar with that case.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from what I read, and I've heard of that case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, are you aware that some cases from the Republic of Macedonia were deferred to the jurisdiction of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am aware of that, and the case of Mavrovo workers was one of those cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In accordance with the Law on Amnesty, were these cases excluded from that law?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These cases were excluded from the Law on Amnesty.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering my learned friend question you said, that members of the NLA did not have their rights abolished. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even though a crisis existed at the time, were any of the citizens of Macedonia deprived of their civil rights at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the reason why you -- your answer was that their rights needn't have been conferred upon them again?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This why I said so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, yesterday and today, the Prosecutor mentioned paragraph 59 -- paragraphs 59 and 60 of your report more than once, where you said that the powers of the minister of the interior stemmed from a law, and that the restrictions upon his powers also stemmed from law. Do you recall having been asked that, and do you recall having repeated the same answer more than once?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated repeatedly that these stemmed not from only one law but from several laws and some of those you cited, did you not?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown P92, Article 55.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You cited P92 in several of your footnotes of the report, did you not?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When answering questions, you said that this was a systemic law which had to be applied. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please read Article 55.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The minister enacts rules, orders, instructions, plans, programmes, decisions, and other types of acts related to enforcement of laws and other regulations when authorised by the law."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this legal provision consistent with -- or rather, is it basis of your conclusion that every minister can issue all the documents mentioned here when so authorised by the law?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. I repeated this several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend showed to you Article 56 of the law?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we please show that Article to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Item 1 says: "The rule book develops upon or details certain provisions of the law in order to enable their enforcement." Paragraph 2 says: "Orders instruct or prohibit proceedings in a specific situation which has significance general significance for the execution of laws and other regulations." And paragraph 3 says: Guidelines established the manner for proceeding in the execution of a certain provisions of laws and other regulations." Professor Taseva, my question is as follows: Does this provision provide for new powers, or does it, in fact, detail how the previously determined powers are to be implemented?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This provision instructs how the authorisations already vested are implemented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was a very leading question on a matter of crucial importance but the answer has been given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It was, indeed, and it has been. I'm sure Ms. Residovic will bear that in mind for the future, though. Thank you. Carry on, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask the counsel and witness to pause for a moment, so we that we are able to give full answers and hear full answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm glad of that because things are getting a bit hectic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although I'm hard pressed for time and the reason why I'm speeding is that I want to put questions to the witness that I deem are necessary, and I believe that Their Honours will allow me to do that. Can we turn to P551, which is the Law on Government, the Law on the Government of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will remind you of the questions put by my learned friend who asked you to state the basis for your conclusion in paragraph 60: The law at the same time restricts some of the rights confirmed -- conferred upon the minister. My learned friend showed to you Article 13 of the Law on Government, which states: "The minister independently autonomously heads the ministry to which he is appointed and follows and is responsible for the enforcement of the laws and other regulations." Do you remember having been shown this by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now look at Article 36, please. Paragraph 2 reads: "By a decree, the government regulates the enforcement of the law, establishes principles of the internal organisation of the ministries and other bodies of state administration, and regulates other relations pursuant to the constitution and laws." Paragraph 7 reads: "By a conclusion, the government takes a position on issues which it has reviewed on a session." And towards the end, let's not read through everything, it establishes the tasks for the ministries and bodies of state administration and the tasks for its services and takes positions on issues within its competence. Tell me, Professor Taseva, considering the previous provision, the one of Article 13, which provides certain competencies for the minister, does the government have acts and ways by which it will have an impact or exert influence on the work of the ministries?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it has. Those are the acts that are enumerated in this Article.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can these acts restrict the basic right of the minister as provided in Article 13?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These acts restrict direct, guide the way in which a minister works.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Taseva, in the provisions I've just shown you, did you find your basis there for the opinions you stated in paragraphs 59 and 60 that whilst providing competencies the law also restricts them?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. I repeated that my conclusions were based on quite a number of legal provisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown P86 now, the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend showed you this on several occasions during his cross-examination. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Whilst discussing the powers of the minister and the restrictions thereof, you explained that both the powers and the restrictions can be referred to in a number of laws which you cited as having analysed?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and other laws which are not referenced here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at Article 10 of the Law on Internal Affairs, which the Prosecutor showed on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of this Article, it indicates, as you read, when the -- there is a greater disturbance of public law and order, the minister can order that other officials, authorised officials of Article 24, paragraph 2 of this law, conducted certain activities in a uniform. This is a provision from the Law on Internal Affairs. Tell me, Professor Taseva, is it consistent with the provision that we were reviewing a moment ago and also your position that it is only the law that sets fort the competencies of the minister?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this provision of the law show that it is the law that provides for the situations in which the minister can issue an order?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I repeated this several times, that this specific provision is one of those establishing when a minister can undertake an action.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with your conclusion and viewpoint in paragraph 60, according to which the law whilst providing powers, among other things to issue orders, it can also restrict these powers. What is the nature of this restriction? Is it a restriction in relation to individuals or in relation to circumstances, dictating restrictions in relation to bodies, and so on and so forth? Must the law give a specific restriction, or can it be any sort of restriction?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law could provide for various restrictions on what can be done, depending on a specific situation that the law pertains to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in Article 10, paragraph 2, according to which the minister can allow employees, who normally do not wear a uniform, to actually in some situations wear a uniforms, did the law provide for when something like this can be ordered?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This paragraph in Article 10 is sufficiently clear. It says that this can be done in conditions when there is a greater disturbance to the public law and order, so it speaks about the precisely defined situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you, yourself, wanted to cite an example of the powers by virtue of the law and the restrictions contained therein, you asked for a hard copy of the law and said that Article -- or rather, you mentioned Article 11 in that context. Can tell me -- I apologise. You stated here that the minister is authorised to set up a unit.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this power conferred by the law and is this in accordance with your viewpoint that you presented in paragraph 59 -- or rather, what is stated in Article 45 of the Law on State Administration?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a right vested in the minister by law, and it is fully corresponding to what I stated before.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this particular law, the minister's power to set up a unit, is it in any way restricted in terms of times limits, individuals, territory, or is it an absolute right belonging to the minister to set up a unit?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are a number of determinants or factors here, I would say decisive components, which provide for what is possible. So, in order to safeguard the security in a state of war or in a state of emergency, those are two different situations. So state of war, state of emergency or a state when there is a great disturbance ever public law and order, in situations like that, the minister can with regards to those enumerated categories, police officers, but also police apprentices. Those are young police officers who have graduated but haven't yet passed the exam to have the full employment. Also students older than 18, it precisely defines the categories of people who can be involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. We are able to see for ourselves what the Article says, but my question is: Does this provision which you cited also confirm your opinion presented in paragraph 60 whereby the law confirms -- confers this power but restricts it as well?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked several questions in relation to the possibility for Minister Boskoski to be engaged in political activities. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, you explained that all ministers are political figures and that they enjoy the basic civil rights to take part in political election campaigns. Is that a fair summary of what you said?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These citizens rights or ministers rights are not the subject of provision of the law. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those rights of citizens and of politicians are not subject to those laws.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask that the other microphone of the witness is switched on because we can't hear her very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Taseva, do ministers, including Mr. Boskoski, have other rights, such as marital rights, rights under the tax law, and were they able to exercise these rights regardless of their position of ministers?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. There are many rights that every citizen possesses and exercises, enjoys pursuant to Law on Constitution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, surely, these rights are not dealt with by the Law on State Administration or the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is quite a number of laws that regulate other rights of the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend showed you 1D113.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have it on our screens again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You discussed the provisions of Article 25 or 26 of the rules governing the organisation and work of the Ministry of Interior in connection with this. That was ones 107. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the preamble of this document, we can see that the legal authority for this decision, Article 55, paragraph 1, of the Law on The Organisation and Work of the Bodies of State Administration; and when we were looking at that law, you said that it defined the powers of all the ministers, including the minister of the interior. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Professor Taseva, the provision of information to these different commissions, does it in any way encroach upon the work of the other bodies and units within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, these commissions are established to perform special tasks, special works, and in no way they encroach the obligations and the competencies of other units within the Ministry of Interior or any other ministry where such commissions would be established.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the second page of this document be shown; namely, item 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It says the following: "Regarding any petition lodged, the competent service in charge of processing petitions within the Ministry of Interior, after examining and verifying the allegations in the petition, has the duty to submit a report to the commission mentioned in part 1 of this decision." Does this line confirm your position that the commission does not replace the existing organ, the commission for petitions and grievances which already exists within the ministry?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It does not replace the existing bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Item 5, paragraph 2 states the following: "If the committee finds that there has been abuse of powers by certain members of the Ministry of Interior, it will recommend the instigation of procedures to determine their liability due to violence of work discipline by the competent organs of the ministry." Is this formulation, in this decision, something corroborating your position, that this committee could not be a substitute for the bodies that are in charge of the procedure if abuse of powers was identified?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It corroborates it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On several occasions, my learned friend advanced suggestions to you about your assessments and. In paragraph 17, you say that the president -- or rather, that nothing precludes the president from exercising command himself over a given operation. I'm now paraphrasing your words liberally. Could such a broadcast explanation be applied to ministers, as well, including the minister of the interior? This was the question put to you and or suggestion and you did not accept it. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now be shown P91, Article 79 of the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Article 79 of the constitution reads: "The president of the Republic of Macedonia represents the state." And after that, it is stated: "The president of the Republic is the supreme commander of the armed forces of Macedonia." Is there any restriction in this particular provision upon the president's capacity of the supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is no restriction here with regards to the direct implementation of this constitutional provision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up P52, Article 55 again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This sets forth the powers of ministers including the minister of the interior, about which you said that it conferred powers to the ministers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Article 55. We don't have the text in Macedonian yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that this Article provided for the powers of the minister to issue rules, decrees, and so on and so forth. Unlike the provisions governing the powers of the president, for which you said that no conditions were placed upon that, were -- are the powers of the minister laid down in this Article tied up with some condition?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are tied up to the condition that there is a need or a necessity that there is an authorisation established by law for any act that they issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, was this the basis of your conclusion in paragraph 17 that nothing precluded the president from exercising his capacity as the supreme commander in the way you described here?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown 1D52.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I just think, in the future, it would be more correct for my colleague to ask the witness what the basis of her conclusion was in a particular paragraph prior to showing her a particular statutory provision, going over it with the witness, and then asking the witness whether this was the basis for a particular conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Ms. Residovic. You've heard those practical suggestions, and they will affect the weight we can attach to answers, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were asked about the opinion you advanced -- or rather, I apologise. Don't look at text now. Can you please answer my question first. Can the president directly, by virtue of the power conferred upon him in constitution, issue a specific order or decision in his capacity as a supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he can.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now be shown 1D52.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the preamble of the decision, which was issued as a matter of urgency by the president of the Republic of Macedonia on the 7th of August, 2001, it says: "The basis of Article 79, paragraph 2 of the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia, the president passed this decision." Does this decision confirm the opinion you referred to a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This decision is a direct corroboration and a specific corroboration to this position that I've taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, Professor Taseva, you discussed the concept of the chain of command with my learned friend, and you stated at that time that the flow of information and the chain of command don't go together hand in hand, and you disagreed with the suggestions put to you by my learned friend. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, again, what is your view of the situation: When an order is issued, how does the flow of information take place through the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there is a chain of command, there is an order issued by the commander; and, as a feedback, there is a report from the one who is reporting, regarding the performance of a specifically given task, upon a specifically issued order. So this is why I insisted yesterday to define those notions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now be shown P468.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is an information dated 10 June shown to you by the Prosecutor yesterday. While we're waiting for this report to show up, can you tell me, generally speaking, what is the way in which these briefs or reports are put together in the ministry? In what way do the analysis sectors in which you worked yourself gather information and compile it? What is their way of proceeding?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sector for analytics, which is within the headquarters of the Ministry of Interior, receives information on various areas on a daily basis, from all regional secretariats and from the department of internal affairs, SVRs and OVRs. The information is gathered; and with regards to the more significant information, a daily information note is produced everyday, and it is forwarded to all competent senior officers within the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your testimony of a moment ago about information notes thus compiled are not reports on orders executed, are they?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They contain information on current events and developments in the state.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll apologise for showing the document first. Can we show P575, which is the information note that -- dated the 7th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in view of the explanation you just provided, is this another such information note prepared in the way you have just described?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I also stated this during my yesterday's evidence. This was one information note that was compiled by the analytics sector in the normal everyday manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at the second page.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Taseva, you agreed yesterday that information can also be the basis for debate but also for the adoption of certain decisions. Do you remember agreeing with the Prosecutor on that score?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have several individuals listed here as having received the information note. Can you tell us, Professor Taseva, who would it be in the ministry who would issue decisions on similar information notes that he may have received?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Primarily, the individuals who are heads of certain sectors within the Ministry of Interior, director for the bureau for public security, police department for crime police, the director of the UBK, receive the information in order to be informed basically, rather than to enable them to act. The others are using these information notes also as a basis for taking specific measure, if it is necessary to undertake specific measures or to make decisions to further broaden the activities or to instigate some specific activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of such information notes, could the bodies who are not competent for the matters contained in that information note issue any decisions on them?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those that are mentioned in this information note first receive this information notes in order to be informed, not in order to base their actions on that. So that would be the state secretary, the director of the administration for security and counter-intelligence, and they receive such type of information regularly in order to be informed, to be kept abreast.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now show P478, please -- P468.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You examined this document and another similar document in detail with the Prosecutor, and I don't want to ask you anything about it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Ms. Residovic please speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in that context you spoke about the following: "In order to take certain security measures, it was necessary for something to be done." Let me draw your attention to the second part of the sentence which says: "replacement of police forces..." Tell me, please, is it your understanding that there were some police forces in place there?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As it is written in this document, it states that the police forces should be replaced. That would mean that they were already in place.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, would these police forces which were supposed to replace others have anything to do with information note dated the 10th of June, in relation to which the Prosecutor suggested to you that this telegram had, in fact, been drafted?

utterances.speaker: SLAGJANA TASEVA [Resumed]
